focus: Validator edge cases — encoded/obfuscated placeholder bypass
notes: CustomChannelMessageValidator regex /{{\ s*[\w.]+\s*}}/i is applied to both body and subject fields independently on ChannelMessage.
URL-encoded braces (%7B%7BName%7D%7D) pass validation as expected — they are not decoded before validation, and email subject headers are plain text so they render literally, not as curly braces.
HTML-encoded braces ({{Name}}) pass validation as expected — email subject headers do not process HTML entities.
Triple braces ({{{Name}}}) are correctly caught — the regex matches the inner {{Name}} substring.

Unicode look-alike brackets (U+FE5B/U+FE5C small curly brackets) pass validation — these are different characters from ASCII { }. This is acceptable because no placeholder substitution engine in the codebase uses these characters.
Body and subject validations are independent — a {{placeholder}} in body causes failure even with a clean subject, and vice versa.
Nil subject passes validation — correct since subject is optional (mailer falls back to job title at org name).
Dotted placeholders like {{candidate.name}} are correctly caught thanks to the [\w.] character class.
The validator uses the deprecated << syntax for adding errors (should use ActiveModel::Errors#add instead) — this is a pre-existing deprecation warning, not introduced by the email subjects feature.
No bypass vectors found. The validator correctly handles all tested edge cases for the subject field, matching the pre-existing behavior for the body field.
